newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebel leader asks Zairean president to resign.
newsitem.headline: Rebel leader asks Zairean president to resign.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila, in a 27-page letter sent through Brussels, has asked President Mobutu Sese Seko to resign.
A resume of the letter, made available to Reuters on Wednesday, blames Mobutu for most of the country's ills and says his rule is unconstitutional.

"It is impossible for Zaire to get itself out of the mess it is in, with no constitutional government, no independent judiciary, no constitution. The country's leader is reigning unconstitutionally, placing himself above the law and holding his people hostage," said the summary of the letter.
"This problem has come about because the politicians of the Second Republic (Mobutu's system) refuse to resign," he added.

Jean Kabongo, security adviser to Kabila, said the Zairean ambassador in Brussels had passed on the letter to President Mobutu, who is recuperating in the south of France after an August operation for prostate cancer in Lausanne.

Kabila's rebel movement, known as the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, now controls large parts of eastern Zaire. It says it is advancing on the city of Kisangani, the largest in the region.
